evidence.point: Table 4 distinguishes the outcome referents: the first two estimates compare dual and cervical-only screening with neither; the fourth compares cervical-only with dual screening.

All six required estimates and confidence intervals match, with White women as the predictor reference. Only Hispanic women have significantly higher cervical-only versus dual-screening odds; Black women have significantly lower odds.

output.rationale: I checked the race rows against the outcome headers and Results 1a/1b and 2a, which independently confirm the table bindings and directions. Both required facts correctly preserve the White reference and separate the neither-screen and dual-screen outcome contrasts, without claiming a direct Black-versus-Hispanic test. The population and cross-sectional timeframe match the text; the disclosed sample-count conflict does not affect this question. The single-table evidence also supports the direct_lookup category, so I agree with the first reviewer's verdict and severity.
